title.value: Guiding The Last Layer in Federated Learning with Pre-Trained Models
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: Guiding The Last Layer in Federated Learning with Pre-Trained Models

extractions.description: The paper explores federated learning (FL) using pre-trained models, focusing on efficient transfer learning techniques from centralized learning. It introduces a two-stage approach: HeadTuning (fitting a classifier) and Fine-Tuning, demonstrating reduced communication and computation costs with improved performance.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: While the paper focuses on improving the efficiency of federated learning, it does not directly address sustainable development goals.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Federated Learning (FL) is an emerging paradigm that allows a model to be trained across a number of participants without sharing data. Recent works have begun to consider the effects of using pre-trained models as an initialization point for existing FL algorithms; however, these approaches ignore the vast body of efficient transfer learning literature from the centralized learning setting

primary_category.justification: The paper does not directly focus on any specific climate or ecologically-related sustainable development category. It focuses on improving Federated Learning algorithms.
primary_category.quote: Federated Learning (FL) is an approach in which a common global model is trained by aggregating model updates computed across a set of distributed edge devices whose data is kept private. We desire to train a federated global model capable of equivalent performance as one trained on the same set of centralized data
